answer: Stop sybils with an ocean lantern orchard: an agent stakes a bond for one orchard row. Each dusk the agent rows a lit lantern across the ocean; wardens time the crossing and log its burn in the row ledger, voiding a row whose crossing is doubled or twice-claimed, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 crossings at 16x: one body rows one lantern, and the burn cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents row once, keep rights.
